TASK ID: independent-set-to-vertex-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Vertex Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Independent Set and TARGET is Vertex Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

TARGET = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-dknpreiy
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py provides SOURCE and TARGET with validate(instance) only. It has NO solvers and NO instance generators.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Before submitting, check your reduction. problems.py has no solvers, so first write your own brute-force solvers for both problems from the definitions above. Then write tests in test_reduce.py that compare your solvers' answers on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise until the tests pass. Finally write verdict.json as {"verified": true or false, "tests_run": <int>, "tests_passed": <int>}, where verified is true only if all of your tests pass. Then submit.
When you submit, an oracle checks reduce.py. If it finds a problem, it replies with a counterexample instead of ending the task (at most 3 times): fix reduce.py and submit again. Each time, verdict.json is cleared: write it again after re-testing.

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Vertex Cover.

Key fact: a set S of vertices is independent (no edge with both endpoints in S)
iff its complement V \\ S is a vertex cover (every edge has at least one
endpoint outside S, i.e. in V \\ S).

Therefore the graph has an independent set of size >= k iff it has a vertex
cover of size <= n - k.  The reduction keeps the graph and maps k -> n - k.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any


def reduce(instance: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Reduce an Independent Set instance to a Vertex Cover instance."""
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]
    return {"n": n, "edges": [list(e) for e in edges], "k": n - k}

from __future__ import annotations
from itertools import combinations


def _has_edge(edges, s):
    for u, v in edges:
        if u in s and v in s:
            return True
    return False


def solve_independent_set(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]
    if k <= 0:
        return True
    if k > n:
        return False
    for size in range(k, n + 1):
        for combo in combinations(range(n), size):
            if not _has_edge(edges, set(combo)):
                return True
    return False


def solve_vertex_cover(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]
    if k < 0:
        return False
    if k >= n:
        return True
    for size in range(0, k + 1):
        for combo in combinations(range(n), size):
            s = set(combo)
            if all(u in s or v in s for u, v in edges):
                return True
    return False
